citations.review_text: The game contrilling is so slow and weird...

I loved the remakes of RE2 and RE3 but just couldn't get into this one. I think it's the combat. It seemed like in RE2 and 3 you'd be facing a few enemies at a time, and choosing the right weapon or making a well-placed shot mattered. Here they throw hordes of enemies at you that may spawn infinitely, and none of your actions seem to matter. Headshots seem to do no more damage than torso shots, the shotgun seems to do little more than the pistol, and between the enemies being bullet sponges and movement being slow/clumsy I'm constantly getting grappled. It's just not fun, and I don't get the hype.

citations.review_text: Very good! just wish there wasn't so much yellow paint everywhere.

i think the atmosphere of the original is transcribed into a modern setting very well, and mechanics like the melee and stun system are adapted pretty wisely into a modern setting as well. the only problem is that on any remotely interactable object in the environment, it's almost guaranteed to have yellow paint (which is a notorious issue with the game to begin with). visual indicators for where players need to go are nice but it needs to be natural signals, not just "oh wow it just so happened that throughout acres of property they could ONLY find yellow paint and on top of that some idiot kept spilling it everywhere that so happens to be important" i also figure that since it's a resident evil game you'd like at least have to figure out where to navigate but with the yellow paint and color scheme splattered on everything remotely important you can probably just turn off your brain and walk through the game. i know that's what i did because on my second playthrough i didn't even remember going through some parts of the game, especially the later chapters (i didnt remember a single thing in chapter 15). the game has a lot going for it but some parts can be lacking compared to the original. the yellow tape/paint thing is pretty bad though

also the game runs fairly well on older systems even if you need to set the game to lower graphics, my computer's fairly weak compared to other modern being a nitro 5 laptop and it held a very consistent 60 fps throughout the ENTIRE game

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game removes quick-time events that were present in the original release.

citations.review_text:
Resident Evil 4 Remake is a great example of how to modernize a classic without losing what made it special. It doesn't try to replace the original. Instead, it refines its ideas, expands its strengths, and delivers an experience that feels familiar while still offering something new.

What impressed me most is how cohesive everything feels. The combat, exploration, resource management, and pacing all support one another, creating a game that is constantly engaging without ever feeling exhausting. Every encounter asks you to think about positioning, ammunition, and risk, making even familiar situations feel rewarding.

The atmosphere is stronger than ever. The environments are rich with detail, and each area has its own identity while maintaining the tension that defines the series. The remake also gives its characters more room to breathe, making both the quieter moments and the larger set pieces more impactful.

I also appreciate that it never loses sight of what made Resident Evil 4 so influential in the first place. It's an action game, but it never forgets its survival horror roots. Resources are limited, exploration is encouraged, and the constant balance between confidence and vulnerability keeps the experience engaging from beginning to end.

Resident Evil 4 Remake succeeds because it respects the original without being constrained by it. It understands why the game became a classic, then builds on that foundation with confidence and care. It's one of the strongest remakes I've played, and an easy recommendation.

An overall improvement over the 2005 game that surpasses it by expanding and polishing what made it so special and unique, as well as sanding out the ♥♥♥♥ bits.

2005 RE4's writing was pretty ass even for the time, and the Remake does a fantastic job of grounding, expanding and fleshing it out in a way that makes you actually care about it this time around. On top of that, the gameplay and graphics were aligned with the 2020's technological capabilities and improvements without sacrificing the original's art direction, gameplay rhythm and creative touches.

Luis benefitted HUGELY from the Remake, as did Ada and other characters. However, what was done with Ashley was amazing. Her dynamic with Leon is genuinely wholesome and her actually wanting to help despite being scared ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, displaying fear but acting her age and the whole writing and plot being cleaned up really did her justice the most.

Also, any remake that removes Quick-Time Events from the original game is an automatic gem to me. ♥♥♥♥ Quick-Time Events. I'm glad this garbage trend mostly remained in the 2000s and 2010s.

citations.review_text:
To be hoenst I wasn't sure if im the person to ask but Having replayed recently I want to go ahead and get my full thoughts out there. This game in itself is a master piece. I honestly never found zombies to be that scary but this game cranks up surival action to a whole new degree. As for each section of the game here are my thoughts individually

Gamplay: Lets get the obvious out of the way. Yes the gameplay is fan fricken tastic. Between being able to shoot, parry, and even round house kick zombies in the face? Why the heck would i not find that satifying to do (Especially since I played 2 remake before this). The ability to kit out whatever guns I want and think work best for me is amazing. I am a fan of being able to kit myself out to how I like to play the game and for the most part the guns each give you that chance whether you want to be a powerhouse, have the best accuracy, etc. I did find myself getting somewhat frustrated but to be honest I was playing the hardest difficulty and really the mistakes were mine and the game punishes you for making mistakes in judgement

Enviroment: The enviorment feels very resident evil (and thats coming from someone who became a recent fan of the franchise), the different areas between the village, to the castle, and then the island feel very haunting and desolate in the terms that it feels like something came, snatched everyone up and replaced them with monsters. Its a difference I did notice compared to the original, cause these enviroments feel much more unnerving and great at keeping you alert. Special note to the underground area as well, definetly wouldn't want to find myself in that area with Verduigo anyday of the week.

Enemies: The enemies definetly can range from average to straight up out of a nightmare. Again I admittedly have never really understood the grand appeal of zombies except for when they come out of left field to scare the pants off me. However when you keep going forward the game ensures to r…

Capcom please stop trolling with the DDA system.  I die one time at sanctuary approach on hardcore with a map flooded with enemies, and when I go to try again it's literally just half the enemies than before?  Seriously??  Imagine some dev being so insecure about a decent player dying one time on hardcore that he implements a system that basically says, "Here you go loser, clearly you couldn't hack it.."  It's the most fedora dev neckbeard mechanic ever

When this game was announced and came out, it was probably the game I was most excited for ever. And while I had fun shooting Ganados and kicking them (as most everyone does), after finishing the game I had a very weird feeling. As if I should like or even love the game, but I never really had that positive feeling at the end. And as more time went on I just felt more conflicted. The combat and gameplay is mostly the same, but otherwise the remake changed or removed almost everything I love about the original game.

OG4 was such an influential game, it's combat and gameplay loop unique, but now has become the norm, not just in the remake but other games too. So essentially the combat (even modernized) isn't specific to this game anymore, and while updated, sometimes it still feels worse than other games or even other RE games. The movement and animation sway gets so annoying, as a cheap way to imitate the gun sway from the OG, but here you have character sway, weapon sway, camera sway, everything sway. I can play with it, even really well, but it's a cheap way of restricting the players in their actions instead of making more complex enemies and encounters.

So with the combat not being unique anymore to this game, what makes the game unique? The story, the characters, the mood, the audio. And 90% of these are a downgrade from the original game, the personality is gone.

This game goes for a more cliche way of depicting horror, with most things being dark, bloody, in your face, instead of the unease with "something is not right." While the music and audio sometimes retains the character, it's mostly been replaced by your regular pompous orchestration. The Chainsaw track being maybe the single exception, being a dramatic and tense track with the guitar imitating that chainsaw.

There seems to be a weird obsession in thinking just because something has personality that it can't be serious and that being serious makes everything automatically better.
It's comm…

citations.review_text: re4 is genuinely one of my favourite resident evil games out there. i absolutely love how it balances horror and action so perfectly. one minute i’m carefully trying to save every bullet i have and the next leon is doing completely unnecessary backflips, roundhouse kicking ganados and somehow making it all look cool xD leon is easily one of my favourite resident evil characters and i absolutely loved seeing him again. ashley honestly surprised me too. i rlly liked seeing how much she grew throughout the game and became more confident as the story went on…even if i had “LEEOONNNN!!!! HELPPPP!!” stuck in my head the entire time T_T luis was such a fun character and every scene with ada is always entertaining. i also have to mention the merchant bc i genuinely think he’s one of the best characters in the game. every time i heard “what’re ya buyin?” i was immediately happy xD i absolutely loved upgrading my weapons, earning pesetas and spending way too long organising my attache case until everything fit perfectly. don’t even get me started on the shooting range either…i may or may not have spent an unhealthy amount of time there trying to get more charms for my attache case T_T i also ended up having way more fun achievement hunting than i expected. professional difficulty definitely made me question my life choices a few times…but cat ears leon made all the suffering worth it >:3 the graphics are gorgeous too, the puzzles were rlly fun and i never felt like the game dragged on or got boring. also…where’s everyone going? bingo? honestly those spanish residents were kinda evil lmao. overall re4 is genuinely one of those games i know i’ll keep coming back to. it’s just an absolute blast from beginning to end. 10/10<3

Throughout the game, the enemies keep hurling axes, sickles, and pickaxes at your head. They've taken aiming to another level—it feels like they have aimbot. It's the best resident evil game that ever been released. However worst for chasing achievements, made me cancer while getting Professional S+ run.

This was my first RE game, and I gotta say, it had a great start with me. The combination of BS cinematic stunts and eldritch horrors that are still within human comprehension is quite interesting. It has a sort of humoristic horror tone to some parts, like, stuff just gets wacky sometimes, but it still feels believable (and spooky), somehow. I also like how it doesn't jumpscare you, ever. It's overall a very solid game, though I have my reservations about the highest difficulty being more frustrating than challenging in many ways. The game has some very intelligent skips and you can see it was cleverly made. It was a huge pain to get all achievements in, but it was very rewarding, and it's a huge flex IMO.
